data.name: Galfridus
data.short_meaning: Friend of the bright or noble one
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old High German 'alf' (elf) and 'frid' (peace), 'Galfridus' signifies 'a friend of the bright or noble one'. In the Middle Ages, it was common for names to reflect the person's relationship with a powerful or spiritual figure, and Galfridus was no exception. With such a noble moniker, one could expect a child named Galfridus to be loyal, steadfast, and devoted.
data.spiritual_meaning: Signifies a connection to the divine, a beacon of light and hope in life.

in_hebrew.name: גאלפרידוס
in_hebrew.meaning: מקור השם הוא באנגלו-סקסוני, פירוש: 'כוח רב' או 'גאולה'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם גאלפרידוס באנגלו-סקסוני, ומשמעותו 'כוח רב' או 'גאולה'. בתקופה הביזנטית, שם זה היה נפוץ ושימש כשם פרטי וכשם משפחה. במסורת הנוצרית, גאלפרידוס נחשב לשם חסיד, ומסמל את האדם החסיד, שאוהב את האל ואת חבריו.

in_greek.name: Γαλφριδός
in_greek.meaning: πηγή το ονομα κατά τους Αγγλο-Σαξονικούς, περιγραφή: 'κρατος πολυς' ή 'αποκάλυψη'
in_greek.long_meaning: πηγή το ονομα Γαλφριδός κατά τους Αγγλο-Σαξονικούς, και σημαίνει 'κρατος πολυς' ή 'αποκάλυψη'. Στην Βυζαντινή εποχή, το όνομα αυτό ήταν γνωστό και χρησιμοποιούνταν ως προσωπικό όνομα και ως επώνυμο. Στην εκκλησιαστική παράδοση, ο Γαλφριδός θεωρείται ως σωτήρας, και αντιπροσωπεύει τον ευσεβή ανθρωπο, που αγαπά τον Θεό και τους συνανθρώπους του.

in_latin.name: Galfridus
in_latin.meaning: originem nomen Anglosaxonico habet, descriptio: 'potentia magnus' vel 'apocalypsis'
in_latin.long_meaning: originem nomen Galfridus Anglosaxonico habet, et significat 'potentia magnus' vel 'apocalypsis'. In aetate Byzantina, nomen hoc erat notum et utbatur ut nomen proprium et ut nomen familiae. In ecclesiastica traditione, Galfridus est consideratus ut salvator, et repraesentat hominem pietate animatum, qui Deum et homines suos amat.

in_english.name: Galfridus
in_english.meaning: Originates from Anglo-Saxon, meaning: 'great power' or 'apocalypse'
in_english.long_meaning: Galfridus originates from Anglo-Saxon, and means 'great power' or 'apocalypse'. In the Byzantine era, this name was widespread and was used as a personal name and as a surname. In Christian tradition, Galfridus is considered a savior, and represents the devout man, who loves God and his fellow man. The name Galfridus is associated with qualities like strength, courage, and a strong sense of justice. It is also linked to the idea of revelation and spiritual awakening.

data.cultural_impact: In the Middle Ages, the name Galfridus was associated with nobility and friendliness, as its Old High German roots hinted at elven origins and a peaceful disposition. It was a popular name for boys in medieval Europe, and many notable figures bore this name, including Galfrid of Monmouth and Galfrid of Le different croissants. Galfridus was considered a sign of good breeding and a useful companion, much like an elfin ally in folklore.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Galfridus also held deep spiritual significance for early Christians, as the name's Old High German roots alluded to a bond between the bearer and a divine being. Galfridus could be seen as a symbol of friendship with God, a reflection of a devout and faithful spirit. In the Christian tradition, the name was an affirmation of the belief that every person is a beloved child of God, worthy of peace, love, and friendship in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference: Galfridus of Monmouth was a medieval Welsh bishop and historian. He is best known for his historical work, the Historia Regum Britanniae. This work, completed around 1136, describes the history of Britain from its mythical founding by Brutus to the establishment of the English monarchy in the reign of Henry I.

Saint Galfrid of Le Mans was a French bishop and martyr. According to legend, he was a disciple of St. Martin of Tours and was sent as a missionary to Brittany. He was captured and tortured by the pagan inhabitants of the region. Eventually, he was beheaded, and his relics were taken to Le Mans, where he is venerated as a saint.
